text:
anya: heads-up, ran the full onboarding battery (kmeans/silhouette + recall@1/5/10 + idflip) for sparkplug-v2-int6 vs v1 on en/fr/de holdouts. seeing a cluster compactness regression and recall dip. anyone available to quick-triage? :wave:

mike: put the numbers here? quick overview is fine.

anya: pasted compressed summary: 

```
model: sparkplug-v2-int6 (per-channel symmetric 6-bit)
holdouts: en/fr/de (10k each)
preproc: same tokenization + centering
whitening: enabled (sparsity-aware)
batching: microbatch=8
metrics:
  recall@1: v1=0.71 -> v2=0.68
  recall@5: v1=0.88 -> v2=0.84
  recall@10: v1=0.93 -> v2=0.90
  silhouette: v1=0.24 -> v2=0.15
  idflip_rate: v1=0.4% -> v2=3.2%

notes: centroid L2 delta (median)=0.098, 90p=0.27, cluster 37 delta=0.62 (de longtail)
```

siva: idflip x8 is alarming. did you run with the same quant calibration seed/data?

anya: calibration used 1000 pooled random examples across languages (not stratified). thought that might be the issue, since the big centroid deltas land on longtail clusters.

karen: i saw something similar on a small probe: channels with very low activation on the calibration set get wildly different scale factors after per-channel calibration, which collapses rare-token subspaces.

mike: can you run two quick follow-ups: (A) stratified calibration (over-sample longtail buckets) and (B) unit-norm postproc (L2 normalize embeddings) so we can separate norm-shift vs angular distortion. Also collect k=100 nn distance histograms intra vs inter.

anya: kicking both off. queued: stratified-calib n=2000 (50/25/25 lang split) and unit-norm-run.

eval-bot: run 1762345679 queued -> results will be posted here when finished. includes per-cluster recall, centroid deltas, nn histograms.

siva: if stratified helps, we should change default calib to stratified for embedding tables and add a small synthetic longtail integration test. calibration should pick samples by token frequency deciles.

anya: quick interim: ran a micro-run (2k samples stratified) on a smaller holdout set (2k docs each). results: recall@5 +1.2 pts, silhouette +0.05 median, idflip down to 1.1%. centroid L2 median delta -> 0.06. still have a few outlier clusters with >0.4 delta.

mike: promising. can you dump per-channel scale histograms (old vs new calib) and highlight channels where scale ratio >2 or <0.5? i suspect those correspond to the problem clusters.

anya: uploaded a small table to the eval report (link internal). excerpt: 

```
channels with big ratio: [12, 47, 203]
channel 47: old_scale=0.0032 new_scale=0.0011 (ratio 2.9)
channel 203: old_scale=0.0007 new_scale=0.0023 (ratio 0.30)
```

karen: that fits: channel 47 is dominated by a handful of high-freq tokens in calibration pool; when we stratified we reduced its influence. channel 203 is rare-token heavy so scale increased and produced larger quant steps -> more noise.

siva: next steps: (1) if stratified recalib consistently recovers recall/silhouette, gate it behind a short PR to quant pipeline with a flag default=on for embedding tables, (2) add a CI eval that simulates longtail (synthetic) to prevent regressions, (3) consider switching per-channel symmetric -> asymmetric for low-activation channels (less clipping).

mike: also run a cosine-eval (unit-norm) against production queries to see if service-level metrics would regress. if unit-norm largely recovers recall, then norm-shift is the main issue and whitening/centering interactions need recheck.

anya: unit-norm micro-run: recall@5 recovered ~0.6-0.8 pts vs v1 but silhouette still lagging on a few longtail clusters. suggests both norm-shift and angular distortion.

anya: plan I'm executing: 
- finish full stratified recalib run (n=10k per holdout) and full NN histograms (k=100)
- dump per-channel scale diffs + synthetic longtail integration test
- if green, open PR to default to stratified sampling and add the test + a canary job
- if partial, loop in siva for per-channel asymmetric quant experiments

mike: ack. please paste the PR link here once opened. if you want i can sketch the test harness.

anya: will do. thx all, updating when the full runs finish (should be ~45m). :coffee:
